title: Basic Grammar (Essential Grammar in Use - Murphy)
lesson_overview: A1 level grammar foundation for beginners, covering the most essential structures for basic communication.

topics.name: Present Simple
topics.focus: Regular and irregular verbs, positive/negative/interrogative forms
topics.lesson_text: Present Simple used for habits, daily routines, permanent situations, and general truths. Structure: I/you/we/they + verb (s/es for he/she/it). Negative: I/you/we/they + do not + verb. He/she/it + does not + verb. Question: Do + I/you/we/they + verb? Does + he/she/it + verb?. Signal words: always, usually, often, sometimes, never.
examples: I usually get up at 7 o'clock.
The sun rises in the east.

topics.name: To Be
topics.focus: am, is, are in present tense
topics.lesson_text: The verb 'to be' is irregular and used for identification, description, and origin. Affirmative: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are. Negative: I am not (isn't), you are not (aren't), he/she/it is not (isn't), we/they are not (aren't). Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he/she/it...? Are we/they...?. Used with adjectives, nouns, and locations.

topics.name: Articles
topics.lesson_text: Indefinite article 'a' used before consonant sounds, 'an' before vowel sounds - for first mention of countable nouns. Definite article 'the' used for specific/known items, unique things, superlatives, 'of' phrases. No article used with uncountable nouns, plural general nouns, sports, languages, meals. Some vs. any in negatives/questions.
examples: A cat is on the roof.

topics.name: Pronouns
topics.focus: subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
topics.lesson_text: Subject pronouns replace noun subjects: I (first person singular), you (second person), he (male third person), she (female third person), it (object/animal/idea), we (first person plural), they (third person plural). Used as the subject of a verb. Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs.

cefr_description: Can use simple phrases and sentences to describe where he/she lives and people he/she knows.
